news.title: New minor risk - Share price stability
news.body: The company's share price has been volatile over the past 3 months. It is more volatile than 75% of Indian stocks, typically moving 8.7% a week. This is considered a minor risk. Share price volatility indicates the stock is highly sensitive to market conditions or economic conditions rather than being sensitive to its own business performance, which may also be inconsistent. It also increases the risk of potential losses in the short term as the stock tends to have larger drops in price more frequently than other stocks. Currently, the following risks have been identified for the company: Major Risk Market cap is less than US$10m (₹546.9m market cap, or US$5.73m). Minor Risk Share price has been volatile over the past 3 months (8.7% average weekly change).

news.title: Investor sentiment deteriorates as stock falls 18%
news.body: After last week's 18% share price decline to ₹33.16, the stock trades at a trailing P/E ratio of 8.7x. Average trailing P/E is 17x in the Luxury industry in India. Total loss to shareholders of 15% over the past three years.

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹0.18 (vs ₹0.34 in 3Q 2025)
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹0.18 (down from ₹0.34 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹596.0m (up 19% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹2.39m (down 48% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 0.4% (down from 0.9% in 3Q 2025). The decrease in margin was driven by higher expenses. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 31% per year but the company’s share price has only increased by 1% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings growth.

news.title: Second quarter 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹1.10 (vs ₹0.012 in 2Q 2025)
news.body: Second quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹1.10 (up from ₹0.012 in 2Q 2025). Revenue: ₹585.7m (up 21% from 2Q 2025). Net income: ₹15.0m (up ₹14.8m from 2Q 2025). Profit margin: 2.6% (up from 0% in 2Q 2025). The increase in margin was driven by higher revenue. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has fallen by 9% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 2% per year, which means it is well ahead of earnings.
